question.title: NEP 53 — Evolving the NumPy C-API for NumPy 2.0

caller.text: A downstream C/Cython extension maintainer building against NumPy headers and distributing a binary extension.

input.text: Downstream extension source, newer NumPy headers and an optional NPY_TARGET_VERSION baseline such as NPY_1_22_API_VERSION; absence of the macro selects a suitably old API by default.

output.text: A binary built with the newer headers that exposes/uses only the selected compatible API surface and runs on the chosen older NumPy baseline; the wider design additionally seeks one rebuilt binary for both NumPy 1.x and 2.0.

limits.text: The bounded action is compile-time API selection for an older baseline. NumPy 2.0 API-table translation, layout changes, downstream source edits and packaging are remaining full-design integration.
Passing state/context for CPython subinterpreters or HPy is not part of this design. Concrete API removals are illustrative and may be reconsidered case by case.

The first design discusses NumPy 1.25 followed by 2.0; Cython 3 could hide struct-layout changes, while supporting Cython 2.x would require downstream macro/Python-object changes. Do not assume either ecosystem transition already occurred.

The initial text reports presentation at a 2023-04-03 planning meeting. No meeting contents or immutable first meeting design were retrieved. The recorded initial_date is the verified numbered-NEP PR creation on 2023-04-13, and both dates remain in the same sampling period.

whole_must.predicate: Compile against newer NumPy while targeting an older API by default, with an explicit target-version selection mechanism and opt-in access to newer API.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Build an extension with newer headers and target NPY_1_22_API_VERSION. If only installing old build headers can target 1.22, the requested new-header build mechanism is absent.

whole_must.predicate: Hide struct fields and API functions introduced after the selected target unless the caller opts into a newer API surface.
whole_must.falsifying_input: At an old selected target, compile source that refers to a field/function introduced only after that target. If the default/old-target headers expose it as usable without opt-in, the gate is falsified.

whole_must.predicate: After recompilation/adaptation against NumPy 2.0, allow one downstream binary to work with both NumPy 1.x and 2.0, rather than requiring two incompatible binary distributions.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Compile one downstream extension against the 2.0 design and import it under the supported 1.x and 2.0 runtimes. Failure on either solely due to the intended cross-version compatibility mechanism falsifies the full migration goal.

whole_must.predicate: Newly compiled downstream extensions must reach compatible runtime implementations when the NumPy C-API/ABI evolves across the supported runtimes; the compatibility integration must not dispatch through incompatible API-table entries.

source_positions.section: NumPy 2 compatibility and API table changes

whole_must.falsifying_input: Import and execute the same rebuilt extension on supported NumPy 1.x and 2.0 runtimes after an API-table change. A call landing at an incompatible function pointer fails the outcome; a correct header-only bridge is not excluded merely for lacking a separate package.

whole_must.predicate: Allow substantive NumPy C-API/ABI evolution through downstream recompilation and documented adaptation, rather than requiring all old binary layouts and exposed API entries to remain frozen indefinitely.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Propose a supported API removal or public-structure change with a documented downstream adaptation. A design that can maintain its compatibility promise only by forbidding every such C-API/ABI change fails the evolution goal.

whole_must.predicate: Manage the C-API break through explicit downstream recompilation and documented replacements/adaptation for removed or changed API, keeping large state/context rewrites outside this proposal.
whole_must.falsifying_input: A downstream extension using a changed/removed C-API entry must have a documented adaptation path after recompilation. Requiring every call to gain an unrelated HPy context, or no replacement guidance for a changed entry, fails the full migration boundary.

partial_must.predicate: Let the caller select the oldest supported NumPy API at compile time while using newer NumPy headers.
partial_must.falsifying_input: With newer headers, request NPY_1_22_API_VERSION. Requiring a separate installation of 1.22 headers instead of honoring the target setting falsifies the partial operation.

partial_must.predicate: Default to an older compatible API and hide newer fields/functions unless a newer target is selected.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Omit the target macro and attempt to reference an API addition newer than the advertised default target; exposure without opt-in falsifies the compatibility gate.

partial_must.predicate: The resulting extension using only the selected API must actually be compatible with that older NumPy runtime; changing a preprocessor label alone is insufficient.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Compile a source that uses only the selected baseline API with newer headers and load it on that baseline runtime. An ABI/import failure caused by the target mechanism falsifies the promised output.

question.independent_partial_purpose: Build a downstream extension using current build headers while retaining an older runtime baseline. This directly removes the need to compile only against the oldest supported NumPy, even before NumPy 2.0 table/layout migration is implemented.
question.remaining_adapter: Set the version macro/build flag and choose a supported baseline in the extension build. Wider 2.0 compatibility still requires descriptor access adaptation, API-table translation/import handling, recompilation and packaging. If the adapter must hide new APIs or implement binary compatibility itself, the returned item has not completed this partial action.
question.same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: CPython Py_LIMITED_API or a Python packaging requires-python marker selects a different actor/API boundary; neither proves compatibility with an older NumPy C-API. A version string printed by a build tool without controlling exported NumPy symbols or resulting binary compatibility also fails.

candidates.name: NumPy NPY_TARGET_VERSION and NPY_FEATURE_VERSION controls
candidates.proposed_use: Configure or inspect the extension's targeted NumPy C-API feature version while using NumPy's import-time runtime-compatibility checks.
